title: 2014 AMC 12B Problem 17
statement: Let \(P\) be the parabola with equation \(y = x^2\) and let \(Q = (20, 14).\) There are real numbers \(r\) and \(s\) such that the line through \(Q\) with slope \(m\) does not intersect \(P\) if and only if \(r \lt m \lt s.\) What is \(r + s?\)

solutions.text:
The line through \(Q\) is \(y = m(x-20) + 14.\) Substituting into \(y = x^2\) gives \[ x^2 - mx + (20m - 14) = 0. \]

There is no intersection exactly when this has no real root, i.e. when the discriminant \(m^2 - 4(20m-14)\) \(= m^2 - 80m + 56\) is negative. That happens between the two roots \(r\) and \(s\) of \(m^2 - 80m + 56 = 0.\)

By Vieta’s formulas, \(r + s = 80.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The line is \(y = m(x-20) + 14;\) set it equal to \(x^2\)
No intersection means the discriminant \(m^2 - 80m + 56 \lt 0;\) use the sum of the roots \(r, s\)
